# DEAL STRUCTURE & TAX PLANNING MEMORANDUM
**Step-Plan & Structural Analysis**
*Prepared: October 3, 2026 | Status: Draft for Discussion*

---

## PRELIMINARY NOTE

No deal-specific input materials were provided. This memorandum therefore sets out a complete framework and step-plan that covers the full decision tree for structure selection, tax elections, rollover mechanics, and earnout design. Bracketed fields **[█]** must be completed once deal parameters are confirmed. The framework is organized so that counsel can move linearly from threshold questions through execution.

---

## PART I — STRUCTURE SELECTION ANALYSIS

### 1.1 The Three Primary Paths

| Feature | Asset Acquisition | Stock Acquisition | Statutory Merger (Forward/Reverse) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tax basis to Buyer | Fresh (FMV) step-up on all acquired assets | Carries over seller's historic basis unless election made | Depends on election; reverse triangular preserves target sub |
| Seller tax character | Ordinary income on recapture; LTCG on goodwill / §1231 | Single capital gain on shares (if individual/pass-through) | Generally capital gain at shareholder level |
| Liabilities assumed | Buyer selects; unknown liabilities generally excluded | All liabilities assumed by operation of law | All liabilities assumed by operation of law |
| Consents & novation | Required for material contracts | Not required (contract stays in entity) | Depends on anti-assignment clauses & change-of-control provisions |
| State transfer taxes | Triggered on real property, titled assets | Not triggered (no transfer of title) | Varies by state; often not triggered on A-reorg |
| Complexity | Higher — schedules of included/excluded assets | Lower — single transfer of shares | Medium — requires board/shareholder vote, filing articles |
| Preferred by | Buyer (basis step-up; liability ring-fence) | Seller (single cap-gain; no recapture) | Either, depending on tax profile and continuity needs |

### 1.2 Decision Factors for **[Target]**

**Step 1 — Entity type of Target:**
- If Target is an S-corporation or partnership → §338(h)(10) or §336(e) election can achieve asset-deal economics inside a stock-deal wrapper → often the optimal path.
- If Target is a C-corporation with high NOL/credit carryovers → stock deal preserves those tax attributes; asset deal loses them.
- If Target is a C-corporation with no meaningful tax attributes → asset deal or §338(h)(10) election (if available) gives Buyer the step-up it needs.

**Step 2 — Liability profile:**
- Known contingent liabilities (litigation, environmental, tax) → asset deal or reverse triangular merger isolates Buyer's subsidiary from parent-level exposure.
- Clean liability profile → stock deal or forward merger acceptable.

**Step 3 — Third-party consent burden:**
- If Target holds government contracts, regulated licenses, or "change-of-control" sensitive customer agreements → stock deal or reverse triangular merger (Target survives as legal entity) minimizes consent requirements.

**Step 4 — State and local tax:**
- Identify states where Target has real property or titled assets; model transfer tax exposure in asset vs. stock scenarios.
- For multi-state operations, compare apportionment implications of a post-closing restructuring vs. immediate asset acquisition.

**Recommended Placeholder Structure (pending deal specifics):**
> **Reverse Triangular Merger** (§368(a)(2)(E)) with a **§338(h)(10) election** if Target is an S-corp or 80%-owned subsidiary, or a **§336(e) election** if Target is a standalone C-corp selling subsidiary — delivering capital gain treatment to Seller and a stepped-up asset basis to Buyer, while preserving the Target legal entity for contract/license continuity.

---

## PART II — TAX ELECTIONS

### 2.1 §338(h)(10) Election

**Eligibility:** Target must be (a) an S-corporation or (b) a corporation that is at least 80% owned by a selling consolidated group or affiliated group filing a consolidated return. Buyer must be a corporation.

**Effect:**
- Target is deemed to have sold all its assets at "Adjusted Grossed-Up Basis" (AGUB) on the acquisition date.
- Seller recognizes gain/loss at the asset level (not on the stock).
- Target's tax history is wiped; Buyer gets a clean entity with FMV basis in all assets.

**Election Mechanics:**
1. Buyer and Seller must jointly execute IRS Form 8023.
2. Deadline: 15th day of the 9th month following the acquisition date (i.e., ~9 months post-close).
3. AGUB formula: `Grossed-Up Basis = (Purchase Price for recently purchased stock ÷ % of recently purchased stock) × 100% + liabilities + other relevant items`.
4. Allocation follows §1060 / residual method (Class I through Class VII).

**Purchase Price Allocation (§1060 / AGUB) — Class Order:**

| Class | Asset Type | Tax Treatment to Buyer |
|---|---|---|
| I | Cash & general deposit accounts | No amortization |
| II | Actively traded personal property; CDs; US govt securities | Capital asset |
| III | Mark-to-market assets; accounts receivable | Ordinary |
| IV | Inventory | Ordinary |
| V | All other assets (PP&E, etc.) | Depreciated over MACRS life |
| VI | §197 intangibles (non-goodwill) | 15-year straight-line amortization |
| VII | Goodwill & going concern value | 15-year straight-line amortization |

**Practice Note:** Classes VI and VII (goodwill) generate the most deferred tax benefit for Buyer; Seller typically seeks to minimize allocation to these classes (ordinary recapture risk on Class VI; capital gain on Class VII). Negotiate allocation in the Acquisition Agreement with a schedule annexed.

### 2.2 §336(e) Election

**Eligibility:** Broader than §338(h)(10) — available when a parent sells ≥80% of a domestic subsidiary's stock, even if Buyer is not a corporation (e.g., private equity fund, individual).

**Effect:** Substantially similar to §338(h)(10) — deemed asset sale at corporate level, step-up to Buyer.

**Election Mechanics:**
1. Seller (parent) makes the election unilaterally on Form 8883 (final Treasury regulations effective 2013, updated 2019).
2. Deadline: Same 9-month rule.
3. Buyer does not need to consent — but Seller should notify Buyer since it affects Buyer's basis.

**Coordination with Purchase Agreement:** Include representation that Seller will (or will not) make §336(e) election; adjust purchase price mechanics if election shifts tax burden.

### 2.3 §754 Election (Partnership / LLC Targets)

If Target is a partnership or multi-member LLC taxed as a partnership:
- A §754 election causes an "inside basis adjustment" (§743(b)) for the acquiring partner equal to the difference between the purchase price and the transferee's share of inside basis.
- **Strongly recommended** for Buyer when purchase price exceeds inside basis (i.e., almost always).
- Made by filing a written statement with the partnership's tax return for the year of transfer.
- **Sticky** — once made, applies to all future transfers; consider anti-abuse provisions.

### 2.4 §83(b) Election (Rollover / Management Equity)

- Required if management receives restricted equity (stock or profits interests) subject to vesting/forfeiture.
- Must be filed within **30 days** of grant date.
- Effect: Locks in ordinary income recognition at current (typically low) FMV; future appreciation taxed as capital gain.
- **Critical deadline — calendar it immediately upon close.**

### 2.5 State Tax Elections

| Jurisdiction | Election | Trigger | Deadline |
|---|---|---|---|
| [State A] | Separate vs. combined reporting | Acquisition creates nexus | Pre-close planning |
| [State B] | Asset transfer tax exemption | Meets "reorganization" definition | File at closing |
| [State C] | Bonus depreciation conformity | Federal bonus depreciation taken | With state return |

## PART III — ROLLOVER MECHANICS

### 3.1 Rationale and Sizing

Rollover equity (management retaining or reinvesting a portion of deal proceeds into the go-forward entity) serves three purposes:
1. Aligns management incentives post-close.
2. Reduces cash required by Buyer at close.
3. Can preserve tax-free treatment for the rolled portion under §351 or partnership contribution rules.

**Typical sizing:** 5%–20% of total deal consideration for control private equity buyouts; sometimes higher in founder-led deals.

**[Transaction-specific rollover %: █%]**
**[Rollover value at closing: $█]**

### 3.2 Structural Mechanics — C-Corp Target

**Option A: §351 Contribution (Preferred for Tax Deferral)**

```
Pre-Close:              Post-Close:
Seller Mgmt             Seller Mgmt
   |                       |
[Target Shares]    →   [Newco/HoldCo Shares]
                           |
                        [Target]
```

- Management contributes Target shares to Newco in exchange for Newco equity immediately before or simultaneously with Buyer's acquisition.
- Qualifies as tax-free under §351 if transferors (management + Buyer) receive ≥80% of Newco stock for property (cash counts for Buyer's portion).
- **Boot rule:** If management receives any cash ("boot") in addition to Newco equity, they recognize gain to the extent of the boot (but not loss).
- **Mechanics at closing:**
  1. Management executes contribution agreement (Target shares → Newco).
  2. Buyer simultaneously contributes acquisition consideration to Newco.
  3. Newco acquires 100% of Target.
  4. §351 exchange documented; Newco files Form 8949 / Schedule D notation.

**Option B: Rollover via Cash Redemption + Reinvestment (Taxable)**

- Management sells 100% of shares at closing (realizes gain), then immediately reinvests specified dollar amount into Newco equity.
- Simpler documentation; management pays tax on full gain but gets clean FMV basis in Newco shares.
- Preferred when management wants clean tax basis going forward (especially if Target has complex basis history) or when §351 control test is in doubt.

**Option C: Profits Interest / Options (for Key Non-Shareholders)**

- Senior employees who are not current shareholders receive profits interests (partnership) or stock options (corp) in Newco.
- Profits interest: Grant at or above current FMV hurdle; no income at grant if structured correctly per Rev. Proc. 93-27 / 2001-43.
- NSO: Ordinary income at exercise; LTCG on subsequent appreciation.
- ISO: No income at exercise (AMT preference); LTCG on sale if holding period met.

### 3.3 Rollover Equity Terms

The following provisions should appear in the Rollover Agreement and Newco LLC Agreement / Shareholders' Agreement:

| Provision | Recommended Position |
|---|---|
| Vesting schedule | Typically 20%–25% per year over 4–5 years; immediate vesting of unvested equity on sale |
| Good leaver / bad leaver | Good leaver (death, disability, termination without cause): full credit for pro-rata vested + buyout at FMV. Bad leaver (cause, voluntary resignation): unvested forfeited; vested bought at lower of cost or FMV |
| Drag-along | Buyer sponsors entitled to drag management rollover holders on any approved sale |
| Tag-along | Rollover holders entitled to tag alongside sponsor on any third-party sale |
| Anti-dilution | Full-ratchet or weighted-average for rollover shares in subsequent financing rounds |
| Put / call rights | Management put at FMV after [5]-year anniversary; Buyer call at FMV on termination |
| Transfer restrictions | Lock-up for [2] years post-close; ROFR thereafter |
| Registration rights | Piggyback rights on any IPO or secondary offering |

### 3.4 Tax Reporting for Rollover

- **Management:** Reports deferred gain on Form 8824 (like-kind or §351 exchange) or Form 8949 (taxable rollover).
- **Newco:** Files Form 8832 (entity classification) if structured as LLC; Form 8023 / 8883 if §338(h)(10) / §336(e) election made at Target level.
- **Payroll / FICA:** Profits interests and restricted equity grants may trigger W-2 reporting obligations; coordinate with HR/payroll.

## PART IV — EARNOUT MECHANICS

### 4.1 When to Use an Earnout

Earnouts bridge valuation gaps when:
- Buyer and Seller disagree on future performance projections.
- Target has lumpy revenue (e.g., contract renewals, pipeline close timing).
- Regulatory approval risk creates uncertainty about post-close operations.
- Seller management is rolling over and needs ongoing performance incentive tied to deal economics.

**[Decision: Is an earnout warranted in this transaction? █ Yes / No]**
**[Proposed earnout amount: $█ (█% of total consideration)]**
**[Earnout period: █ years post-close]**

### 4.2 Earnout Metrics — Selection

| Metric | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Simple; hard to manipulate via accounting choices | Buyer can sandbag by withholding resources or delaying orders |
| EBITDA | Aligns with Buyer's financing metrics | Subject to accounting manipulation; ambiguous add-backs |
| Gross Profit | Less susceptible to overhead allocation disputes | May not reflect true business health |
| Milestone / Binary | Clear; no dispute about calculation | All-or-nothing creates cliff risk and perverse incentives near deadline |
| Free Cash Flow | Most economically pure | Complex; Buyer controls capex decisions |

**Recommended:** Dual metric — **Revenue floor** (to protect Seller from Buyer underinvestment) + **EBITDA cap** (to protect Buyer from inflated top-line at margin sacrifice). Alternatively, a single **Gross Profit** metric minimizes below-the-line accounting disputes.

### 4.3 Earnout Calculation Mechanics

```
Earnout Payment = MAX(0, MIN(Max Earnout Cap, ((Actual Metric - Threshold) / (Target - Threshold)) × Max Earnout))
```

**Example (illustrative):**
- Max Earnout: $[█]M
- Threshold (0% payout): $[█]M revenue
- Target (100% payout): $[█]M revenue
- Cap (no further upside beyond): $[█]M revenue

| Actual Revenue | Earnout Payment |
|---|---|
| Below $[Threshold] | $0 |
| $[Threshold] – $[Target] | Pro-rata, linear |
| At or above $[Target] | $[Max Earnout]M (capped) |

### 4.4 Earnout Protective Covenants

**Seller must negotiate the following protections in the Purchase Agreement:**

1. **Separate Books:** Buyer shall maintain Target's business as a separate reporting unit for purposes of earnout calculation.
2. **No Sandbagging:** Buyer shall operate the business in a manner reasonably consistent with past practice and its own business plans; shall not take actions primarily intended to reduce the earnout payment.
3. **No Shifting of Revenue/Costs:** No inter-company transactions that shift revenue out of or allocate above-market costs into Target without Seller's consent.
4. **Change of Control Acceleration:** Full or pro-rata earnout payment triggered if Buyer sells Target before end of earnout period.
5. **Audit Rights:** Seller's accountants may audit earnout calculations within [60] days of delivery of the earnout statement.
6. **Dispute Resolution:** Expert determination by an independent accountant (KPMG / Deloitte / PWC or their equivalent) within [30] days of notice of dispute; expert's determination final and binding.
7. **Escrow / Security:** Earnout amounts to be deposited in escrow or secured by letter of credit if Buyer's credit is uncertain.

### 4.5 Tax Treatment of Earnouts

**For Seller:**

- **Installment Sale Treatment (§453):** Earnout structured as contingent payments qualifies for installment reporting — Seller defers a portion of gain until payment received.
  - *Stated Maximum:* If there is a cap on total contingent payments, use the cap as the "selling price" for installment reporting.
  - *No Stated Maximum:* Seller must use 120% of the §1274 AFR to discount the contingent obligation, or elect out of installment treatment.
  - **Election Out of Installment (§453(d)):** Sometimes preferable if Seller expects tax rates to rise, or if Seller has offsetting losses.

- **Character:** Earnout payments generally carry same character as the underlying sale (capital gain on stock; mix of ordinary/capital on assets).

- **Recapture Risk:** §1245 / §1250 recapture must be recognized in Year 1 to the extent of depreciation previously claimed — cannot be deferred via installment method.

**For Buyer:**

- Contingent purchase price that is ultimately paid is capitalized into the purchase price (and allocated per §1060 residual method at that time).
- If earnout is not paid, Buyer reduces its basis in the acquired assets accordingly.
- **GAAP Note:** Under ASC 805, contingent consideration is fair-valued at acquisition date and remeasured each period — creates P&L volatility. Work with auditors early to structure earnout in a way that minimizes remeasurement noise (e.g., milestone triggers that are not subject to fair-value remeasurement).

## PART VI — KEY RISKS AND MITIGATION

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| §338(h)(10) election unavailable (e.g., Buyer is LLC not taxed as corporation) | Medium | High — lose step-up | Consider §336(e) election; restructure Buyer entity pre-signing |
| §83(b) election missed (30-day deadline) | Low | Very High — entire vesting gain becomes ordinary income | Calendar alert Day 1; task partner and associate to confirm filing |
| Earnout dispute (accounting methodology disagreement) | High | Medium | Pre-agree GAAP definitions, permitted adjustments, and specific accounting policy elections in the Purchase Agreement; annex accounting principles exhibit |
| Management rollover fails §351 control test | Low | High — recognition of gain on rollover | Confirm ≥80% test with tax counsel pre-close; use Option B (taxable reinvestment) as fallback |
| State transfer taxes underestimated | Medium | Medium | Commission state-by-state transfer tax study in diligence; budget for worst case |
| HSR second request (if thresholds exceeded) | Low–Medium | High — delay of 3–6+ months | File early; prepare premerger notification well in advance; engage antitrust counsel Day 1 |
| NOL limitation under §382 (stock acquisition of loss corporation) | Medium | Medium | Model §382 annual limitation; consider whether step-up election (§338/§336(e)) renders issue moot |
| GAAP earnout fair-value remeasurement volatility | Medium | Medium | Structure earnout as a milestone (non-financial CPs where possible) to qualify for non-remeasurable treatment under ASC 805 |
